summary.headline: IDFC First Bank Q2 FY27 PAT rose to INR1,045 crore (up ~196% YoY) on FCNR(B) mobilisation of INR34,390 crore, with NIM down to 5.58%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 profit was INR1,045 crore, the second straight quarter above INR1,000 crore, and core PAT (ex-trading and one-offs) was about INR1,036 crore versus INR897 crore in Q1. The bank mobilised USD3.6 billion (INR34,390 crore) of FCNR(B) deposits under the RBI scheme, equal to about 10% of deposits, and extended about INR25,000 crore of FCNR-backed loans to NRI customers. Loans grew 30.1% YoY including FCNR-backed loans (22.2% excluding them), and total deposits grew 25.9% YoY. NIM fell to 5.58% from 5.90% (ex tax refund), which management attributed mainly to the FCNR balance-sheet expansion, and management guided NIM back to about 5.8% by Q4. Gross NPA improved to 1.32% from 1.51%, and credit cost eased to 1.38% from 1.53%.

segments.name: Retail, agri and MSME
segments.commentary: GNPA improved to 1.24% from 1.4% (1.36% ex FCNR-backed loans); retail SMA-1 and SMA-2 fell to 0.72% from 0.77%. Retail current-bucket collection efficiency stable around 99.5%.

segments.name: Wholesale and business banking
segments.commentary: Grew faster than the book, individually more than 30% YoY, and was a driver of the asset-mix NIM drag of 5 bps. Corporate book is about 20% of loans (up from about 15% two years ago), per management's answer to a question. Corporate cost-to-income about 32-33% and yield about 9.2%.

segments.name: Mortgage
segments.commentary: Mortgage GNPA rose to 1.54% from 1.27% over the year; management attributed it to normal book ageing as the book is not being pushed (yield is low).

segments.name: Credit cards
segments.commentary: Outstanding book INR9,875 crore with 5 million cards in force; credit card GNPA fell to 1.49% from 1.99%, while SMA rose to 1.49% from 1.35%.

guidance_outlook: NIM expected to range-bound in Q3 from current levels and recover to about 5.8% by Q4 FY27, driven by excess liquidity deployment (7 bps drag reverses), day count (about 8 bps per management) and repo hikes.

Management assumes repo rate hikes of 25 bps already done, plus 25 bps in the remainder of FY27 (likely December) and 25 bps in April 2027. Blended FY28 cost of funds expected to rise about 5-10 bps over FY27.
Management expects FY27 cost-to-income ratio of about 55% on an incremental basis, with operating jaws of at least 500 bps (H1 jaws 553 bps; Q2 592 bps).
Credit cost guidance referred to as 1.5% to 1.6%; management said it is comfortable for the next couple of quarters, with El Nino risk to be watched in Q3-Q4.
FCNR scheme estimated to add about 100 bps benefit on INR35,000 crore cost of funds versus domestic alternatives; ROA impact of FCNR margin dilution estimated at only about 2 bps.
Management stated loan growth of at least 20% and deposit growth of about 20-22% are visible; LDR expected to stay flat or improve, with deposit flows slightly above loan growth.

IRDAI commission consultation paper could reduce fee income; management expects it to be broadly offset by repo hikes, FCNR benefit and product mix changes. Expected to come into effect from next year.
Operational risk RWA guidelines effective April 1, 2027 expected to offset ECL transition capital impact, leaving CET1 broadly neutral; further clarity expected in about a quarter.
capex_capacity: No new capex plan or branch-expansion figure was given. Management referred to the network of about 1,200 branches and 1,243 ATMs as a cost drag on the liability side.

FCNR(B) raise of USD3.6 billion (INR34,390 crore) was about 2.7% of national mobilisation under the RBI scheme; debut USD950 million bond raised from the offshore IBU; S&P and CareEdge gave investment-grade ratings.
Management said no pipeline for further foreign borrowings (ECB) as the borrowings have largely been mobilised.
Capital raise is under consideration depending on market conditions; not included in the 5.8% NIM outlook.
demand_pricing: Loan growth 30.1% YoY including FCNR-backed loans, 22.2% excluding them. Growth drivers were mortgage, vehicle, consumer loans, and business banking and wholesale (each above 30% YoY).
Deposit growth 25.9% YoY; bank deliberately slowed core deposit growth (ex FCNR 14.1% YoY) and repaid about INR5,000 crore of bulk deposits and about INR5,000 crore of maturing CDs in September.

FCNR(B) deposits cost about 6.85% annualised; management pegs the all-in cost of funds on these at about 6.8-6.85%, versus about 7.8% for domestic equivalent (including CRR/SLR costs), about 100 bps benefit.
Savings account rate cut: management said the bank moved from 7% to 6.5% to 6.25% and now pays 6% above INR25 lakh balances.
About 60% of the book is fixed-rate (including FCNR), about 31-32% repo-linked, and the balance MCLR-linked.

Corporate book: A-and-above rated are 76% of the book, with BBB at 20% and BB and below at 4%; net book about INR70,000 crore against about INR1 lakh crore total exposure including non-funded. Management cited nil delinquency in 7 years apart from one ATM company loss of about INR100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Akshay Jain (Autonomous): Why no visible funding-cost benefit from strong FCNR inflows, and how is the INR34,000-odd crore being deployed; what spread sits behind the 7 bps liquidity drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Sudhanshu said about INR5,000 crore of bulk deposits and about INR5,000 crore of maturing CDs were repaid in September, with excess liquidity parked in low-yielding treasury and nostro balances (LCR 139% in September, normalising to about 115-116% within a month). The 7 bps drag is expected to vanish by Q4. Management cited the savings rate cut (7% to 6%, above INR25 lakh) and guided blended FY28 cost of funds up about 5-10 bps over FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Akshay Jain: Is the 150-160 bps credit cost guidance right, and what is being seen on El Nino, oil and macro?
qa_highlights.answer: Vaidyanathan said 0-30 DPD data show no problem yet and that the bank is comfortable for the next 1-2 quarters; El Nino and drought in Maharashtra and Karnataka will be watched in Q3-Q4. He confirmed that credit cost of 1.5-1.6% is reasonable.

qa_highlights.question: Akshay Jain: Why did mortgage GNPA rise and credit card SMA inch up?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage GNPA went from 1.27% to 1.54%, attributed to normal book ageing with the book not being pushed given low yield and near-nil YoY growth. Credit card GNPA fell from 1.99% to 1.49%, while card SMA rose from 1.35% to 1.49%, described as normal quarter-to-quarter variation.

qa_highlights.question: Param Subramanian (Investec): Is 55% incremental cost-to-income a multi-year commitment, and what is the steady-state liability drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Vaidyanathan said 55% is firmly expected for FY27 and H2, and depends on the roughly 500 bps gap between income and opex growth held for three quarters. On liabilities, he put the current drag at about 0.7% of average retail liabilities (about INR1,500 crore net of tax) and expects it to fall toward zero over about 3 years, with asset ROA of 1.3% seen rising.

qa_highlights.question: Param Subramanian: Confirm the NIM waterfall, Q3 and Q4 path, and asset-mix effect.
qa_highlights.answer: Sudhanshu said a 25 bps repo hike has already happened and one more is assumed in the next quarter; about 32% of the book is repo-linked. Q3 NIM should be range-bound, with recovery to about 5.8% in Q4 from the 7 bps liquidity drag reversing, 8 bps day-count benefit, and repo hikes. Vaidyanathan said the 2-quarter view already factors in asset mix.

qa_highlights.question: Piran Engineer (CITIC): Does September NIM lag the Q2 average, and is the 5.8% guidance excluding a capital raise? Also, why has CASA growth slowed?
qa_highlights.answer: Sudhanshu said September NIM was slightly lower due to high LCR, but Q3 should be range-bound before picking up in Q4. The 5.8% guidance excludes any capital raise, which would be additive. On CASA, average CASA growth is about 23% YoY; Vaidyanathan said the bank intends to hold CASA in the high 40s.

qa_highlights.question: Piran Engineer: What is the corporate book's composition, rating profile and ROA case versus retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Vaidyanathan said A-and-above rated make up 76% of the corporate book, BBB 20% and BB-and-below 4%. Net book is about INR70,000 crore against about INR1 lakh crore including non-funded. Only one ATM company loss of about INR100 crore in 7 years. Corporate cost-to-income is about 32-33% and yield about 9.2% (corrected from 9.5%), implying ROA of 1.6-1.7% at nil credit cost.

qa_highlights.question: Abhishek Murarka (HSBC): Are the insurance commission impacts fully offset by FCNR savings and rate hikes, and what is the quantum?
qa_highlights.answer: Vaidyanathan said management assumes the 25 bps hikes already done plus 25 bps more in FY27 and 25 bps in April 2027, and expects FCNR benefit and product changes to offset the insurance impact. He declined to give a quantum. Sudhanshu put FCNR-related fee income at about INR30 crore and opex at about INR60 crore in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Jai Prakash Mundhra (ICICI Securities): Any further ECB pipeline, LDR outlook, fixed/repo split, and ECL transition impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no further foreign borrowing pipeline. Deposit flows will be slightly above loan growth, so LDR should stay flat or improve. About 60-62% of the book is fixed (including FCNR), 31-32% repo-linked and the balance MCLR. Sudhanshu said the revised operational-risk RWA rules effective April 1, 2027 should broadly offset ECL capital impact on CET1, with more clarity in about a quarter.

risks_watch: El Nino and drought in Maharashtra, Karnataka and other states: management says no impact yet but Q3-Q4 is the watch window for rural and retail stress; credit cost guided at 1.5-1.6%.

NIM path: Q3 range-bound, recovery to about 5.8% in Q4 depends on repo hikes (two assumed, one in December and one in April 2027), excess liquidity deployment and the day-count benefit; FCNR repricing and funding cost rise could offset it.
IRDAI commission consultation could reduce fee income; offsets (repo hikes, FCNR benefit, product mix) are not quantified by management, and the regulation is expected to take effect next year.
Mortgage GNPA rose to 1.54% from 1.27% YoY and card SMA rose to 1.49% from 1.35%; watch whether these trends continue.
CASA ratio fell to 47.6% (average 48.4%) with FCNR in the denominator; management says it aims to keep it in the high 40s, and average CASA growth slowed to about 23% YoY.
Corporate and wholesale book growing above 30% YoY, now about 20% of loans; a single ATM-company loss of about INR100 crore is the only delinquency cited in 7 years.
Capital: CET1 13.01%; a capital raise is under consideration but excluded from the 5.8% NIM outlook; ECL transition and the April 2027 operational-risk RWA rules are still being fine-tuned.
key_quotes: So I can safely say that the trajectory is fairly established by now.
So we feel that we can reasonably give or take, stay in this zone for the next few quarters as well.
As of now, our data numbers don't seem to suggest that there is a problem coming.
We're actually seeing credit card costs coming down actually.
We have no intention of raising more money for fixed deposits and treading the P&L so finally that we let go of the CASA percentage down to the 40s and below 40s.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability, the cost-to-income trajectory and FCNR economics, with management repeatedly pre-empting NIM and ROA concerns. More cautious and non-committal on El Nino, the insurance commission impact (no quantum given) and the ECL transition, which it says is still being fine-tuned.

growth.why: Management guides NIM back to about 5.8% by Q4 FY27 and a 55% FY27 cost-to-income ratio, with loan growth of at least 20% and deposit growth of 20-22% described as visible. Backing is partial: loan and deposit visibility is asserted with no specific capacity or order numbers, and the NIM recovery relies on liquidity deployment, day count and repo hikes.
